Some are hitting the stage for the first time in their lives and others are returning after a 10 year hiatus. Dance is a healing modality – and in our current socio-political state, learning our bodies and encouraging authentic expression will be strengthen our heart, mind and soul. With your support, we plan to open a dance & movement studio in Tacoma for adults (and teens!) in 2027. big_desc: From the producers of the hit 60s Flashback Show comes A Very Merry Christmas Show — a spectacular, all-new holiday celebration filled with music, memories and Christmas magic! Featuring more than 20 of the Northwest s favorite vocalists and an incredible cast of dancers, A Very Merry Christmas Show takes audiences on an unforgettable journey through Christmas past to present — from the beloved songs and traditions of the 1940s and 50s, through the unforgettable Christmas television specials of the 60s and 70s, and all the way to the holiday favorites we love today. Expect soaring vocals, show-stopping dance numbers, dazzling costumes, heartwarming nostalgia and treasured memories of Christmases gone by — all brought to life in the same high-energy, nostalgic style audiences loved in 60s Flashback. After sold-out performances in Seattle, this much-loved holiday production is coming south for one special night at the Federal Way Performing Arts & Events Center. And the magic doesn t end when the curtain comes down! Santa Claus will be waiting in the lobby after the show to meet the kids, making this a Christmas memory the whole family can share. This year, A Very Merry Christmas Show is also proud to partner with local charity PB&J for the Homeless. Guests are invited to join in the spirit of giving by bringing a jar of peanut butter or jelly to donate in the lobby on the night of the performance. Kick-start your Christmas spirit with an unforgettable night of music, dancing, laughter, nostalgia and holiday magic for the whole family. And be ready for a magical finale you won t soon forget.

Mortimer rushes to tell Abby and Martha before they stumble upon the body themselves, only to learn that the two women aren t just aware of the dead man in their parlor, they killed him! big_desc: A season finale is a celebration. Rhythm & Revelry begins with sacred joy in Omar Thomas Come Sunday, a tribute to the Hammond organ s central place in Black worship. The first movement, Testimony, prepares the spirit with a sound world shaped by Bach, blues, jazz, and R&B. The second, Shout!, bursts into the ecstatic moment when celebration takes over. Thomas writes with love, energy, and purpose, honoring Black culture through music that sings, moves, and lifts the room. From there, the spotlight turns to violinist Nathan Amaral in Tchaikovsky s Violin Concerto. Born in Rio de Janeiro, Amaral began violin through a social project in Mangueira and has since become one of the most compelling young violinists on the international stage. He won First Prize at the 2024 Sphinx Competition and the Grand Prize of the 2024 CAG-YCAT Competitions, and Yo-Yo Ma has praised his rare ability to move beyond technique into the heart of musical expression. Ravel s Boléro begins with a single rhythm and one unforgettable theme, repeating again and again as the music grows from a whisper to a blaze. Each section of the orchestra gets its moment to shine, turning one simple idea into a thrilling display of color and control. Strauss Der Rosenkavalier Suite brings the afternoon to a lavish close. Drawn from his beloved opera, the suite mixes romantic sweep with elegant waltzes and the glittering richness of Vienna imagined through Strauss 20th-century orchestral voice. title: Auburn Symphony Orchestra: Symphonic Stories
venue_name: Federal Way Performing Arts & Event Center
description: Auburn Symphony Orchestra: Symphonic Stories
big_desc: Some forces are invisible, but you feel their pull. Symphonic Stories brings together three works about distance, memory, imagination, and the stories that hold us together. A voice reaches across grief. A soloist moves through shifting celestial worlds. A woman tells story after story, surviving one night at a time. Jennifer Higdon s blue cathedral begins the journey in a place of remembrance. Written after the death of her brother, Andrew Blue Higdon, the piece imagines a vast sacred space filled with light, crystal, and upward motion. The flute, Higdon s instrument, and the clarinet, her brother s instrument, move through the music like two voices reaching toward one another. It is a work of loss, but also of release: a quiet ascent through memory toward something larger. From there, Auburn Symphony looks outward with the Co-Commission of Gravity at a Distance, a new saxophone concerto by Viet Cuong written for Timothy McAllister. The concerto takes inspiration from celestial bodies and the unseen forces that bind them across immense distances. The solo saxophone moves through orchestral worlds that feel luminous, floating, dense, and immense, tracing a path between isolation and attraction, stillness and motion. Then comes one of music s great storytellers. Rimsky-Korsakov s Scheherazade draws from One Thousand and One Nights, where Scheherazade survives a violent ruler not through force, but through intelligence, wit, and imagination. Each night, she tells a story compelling enough to earn another dawn. In the orchestra, her voice returns through the solo violin: persuasive, resilient, and unbroken. With blue cathedral, Gravity at a Distance, and Scheherazade, Symphonic Stories becomes a concert about what connects us across silence, space, and danger. These are stories of remembrance, invention, and survival, told in the language of the orchestra.

title: Coffee with the CEO
description: Our next chapter at Tacoma Arts Live is about more than performances. big_desc: UP for Arts and the Concerts in the Atrium series present cellist Sarah Rommel and pianist Carlin Ma in concert on Saturday , November 7, 2026 , at 7:00 PM . Held at the Civic Atrium at University Place Library, this free public performance showcases a dynamic program exploring themes of heritage, friendship, and neoclassicism. The duo will perform Igor Stravinsky s Suite Italienne, a distilled duo version of his neo-Baroque ballet Pulcinella, alongside Indian-American composer Reena Esmail s Jhula Jhule, a poignant tribute to her family s musical traditions. The program also features Benjamin Britten s Cello Sonata, composed for his close friend Mstislav Rostropovich, in a performance commemorating the 50th anniversary of Britten s death. About the Artists Sarah Rommel , cello, is the founder and Artistic Director of Seattle s Jigsaw Chamber Ensemble and a prizewinner of the George Enescu International Cello Competition. She has performed internationally with prestigious ensembles including the Orpheus Chamber Orchestra, East Coast Chamber Orchestra, and Musicians from Marlboro, and holds degrees from the Curtis Institute of Music and the USC Thornton School of Music. Carlin Ma , piano, is an interdisciplinary artist specializing in piano performance, photography, and filmmaking. She has performed at the Kennedy Center, Ravinia, and Tanglewood, serves as Artistic Director of the Hawaii International Music Festival, and has completed visual commissions for Meta and The New York Times. She holds degrees from Indiana University and the San Francisco Conservatory of Music. UP for Arts is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to expanding access to the visual and performing arts within the U.P. community through public concerts, art installations, and community outreach programs. Learn more at upforart.org.

Lecture 6 | Dale Chihuly

How Tacoma s own Chihuly brought Studio Glass into the global imagination, inspiring countless artists and redefining glass as large-scale public art.

In celebration of America s 250th anniversary in 2026, and in partnership with America 250, Forged in Fire at Museum of Glass will combine illustrated lectures, live glassblowing demonstrations, and multimedia content to trace the evolution of American glassmaking, from colonial Jamestown to the contemporary works of Dale Chihuly. Each event illuminates the artistry, design, and cultural significance of glass as both a decorative and functional medium. Forged in Fire will reach diverse audiences throughout the Puget Sound region and beyond via in-person events and live streams, and build community pride in the region s unique role in the American Studio Glass Movement — a movement co-founded by Tacoma-native Dale Chihuly. By combining history, artistry, and live craft, this program exemplifies how decorative arts can spark curiosity, fuel discovery, and create shared cultural experiences.

Lectures and Demonstrations

Museum of Glass will host six unique public sessions pairing glass history talks by renowned glass artist and historian Walter Lieberman with live demonstrations by the Museum s internationally acclaimed Hot Shop Team. Each lecture focuses on a specific period of time in glassmaking history and is accompanied by a demonstration that recreates period-specific objects and techniques, giving audiences tangible insight into the evolution of glass as a decorative art form. All lectures will take place on select Saturdays 1pm in the Museum of Glass Hot Shop. The glassmaking demonstrations will follow at 2pm.

The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra is a dynamic and innovative ensemble committed to providing high-quality performances and music education to communities worldwide. Through a blend of concerts, workshops, compositions, recordings, and cultural exchanges, the orchestra brings people together through the universal language of music, with a special emphasis on the rich traditions of jazz.

Led by saxophonist, composer, and educator Kareem Kandi, the orchestra draws on his vast experience as a performer who has earned acclaim for his work in jazz, blues, classical, and funk. A native of the Pacific Northwest, Kareems versatility as a saxophonist and composer has taken him across the U.S. and around the globe, captivating audiences and critics alike. Known for his ability to honor the traditions of the past while forging new creative pathways, Kareems compositions and unique arrangements of timeless American standards continue to push musical boundaries.

Since 1996, Kareem has performed as both a bandleader and sideman, sharing the stage with luminaries such as Patti Labelle, Ali Jackson, George Colligan, Pete Christlieb, Bill Watrous, The Seattle Symphony, The Paperboys, The Temptations, The Four Tops, and many more. His work with The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra featuring embodies a sound that is fresh, innovative, and appeals to a diverse range of audiences. Each member brings decades of experience and mastery of their instruments, contributing to a performance that transcends genres and connects with listeners on many levels.

About Ali Jackson:

Ali Jackson has performed and recorded with a multitude of artists including Wynton Marsalis, Jon Batiste, Willie Nelson, Tony Bennett, Faith Hill, Karriem Riggins, Bobby McFerrin, Buster Williams, Norah Jones, Eric Clapton, Dee Dee Bridgewater, Aretha Franklin, George Benson, Harry Connick, Jr., KRS-1, Marcus Roberts, Joshua Redman, Vinx, Seito Kinen, Seiji Ozawa, Diana Krall, Gerald Albright, Michael Heise, Russell Gunn, James Morrison, Craig Handy, Jacky Terrasson, Kurt Rosenwinkel, and the New York City Ballet.

As a bandleader, Ali has recorded five albums, including Amalgamations, Wheelz Keep Rollin , Big Brown Getdown and the Yes! Trio album. Ali s playing is featured on more than 40 other albums, including Congo Square, Touchdown, Gunn Fu, Young Gunn Plus, European Sessions, Live at Yoshi s, Reflections in Change, Back East, Two Men With The Blues, Three-Five, Here We Go Again: Celebrating the Genius of Ray Charles, He and She, The Magic Hour and From the Plantation to the Penitentiary. Jackson also collaborated with jazz greats Cyrus Chestnut, Reginald Veal, and James

Carter on Gold Sounds, an innovative album that sought to transform songs by indie alternative rock band Pavement into unique virtuosic interpretations with the spirit of the church and the attitude of the juke joint. His production skills can be heard on George Benson s album Irreplaceable. He is also the voice of Duck Ellington, a character in the Penguin book series Baby Loves Jazz.

Ali is also an acclaimed composer whose voice is unique in its command of the universal language of the groove and the power of thoughtful use of space — both rhythmically and harmonically. His most recent masterworks include the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra-commissioned Living Grooves: A World in Jazz Rhythm and a ballet composed for the Alvin Ailey Dance Company titled r-Evolution, Dream.

Ali s collaborations with other artists continue to push the envelope of jazz music and its connection to the human spirit. In 2010, Ali executive produced an original work called Beats of NYC, a project blending the musical idioms of Congolese, Senegalese, Tap, and modern dances juxtaposed with various styles of spoken word and the history of the blues. He also composed a ballet with long-time collaborator Hope Boykin titled Ballet: Watching go by the Day.

title: Jeremy McCombs Christmas Cowboy Style Tour
description: Jeremy McCombs Christmas Cowboy Style Tour A Traditional Western Christmas Experience Before Christmas became flashing lights, crowded shopping malls, and endless wish lists, it was about something more simple Jeremy McCombs Christmas Cowboy Style brings that spirit back to the stage with an authentic celebration of the American West and the timeless music of the Christmas season. Inspired by the Western Christmas traditions of Michael Martin Murphey, Asleep at the Wheel, Willie Nelson, Lyle Lovett, and the great cowboy storytellers, this one-of-a-kind holiday production blends classic Christmas favorites, Western swing, cowboy poetry, heartfelt storytelling, and the kind of music that feels like coming home. Led by Nashville recording artist and songwriter Jeremy McComb alongside a world-class group of musicians, the show captures the warmth of an old-fashioned Christmas gathering-where the stories mean something, the songs feel familiar, and the spirit of the season takes center stage. This isnt another flashy holiday production. Its a celebration of the Christmas traditions that have been passed down through generations, filled with laughter, beautiful musicianship, nostalgia, and a little cowboy charm. Whether you grew up with cowboy Christmas records playing in the living room or youre discovering these traditions for the first time, Christmas Cowboy Style is a night meant to be shared with the people who matter most. Some Christmas presents dont fit under a tree. Some become memories youll carry for years.

description: A singer-songwriter known for his lyrical acumen and plaintive harmonica style, Joe Pug dropped out of college and moved to Chicago where he worked as a carpenter before breaking into the citys music scene. Paste Magazine wrote of his music: Unless your surname is Dylan, Waits, Ritter or Prine, you could face-palm yourself to death trying to pen songs half as inspired. His music has appeared on NPRs Prairie Home Companion and Mountain Stage . His music has been released by Lightning Rod Records, which features an alumni roster of Jason Isbell, Billy Joe Shaver, and James McMurtry. Additionally, he is the creator and host of the popular podcast The Working Songwriter.

big_desc:
Junior Community Scientists

Ever wondered what it s like to participate in community science projects? Join Communities for a Healthy Bay for a hands-on half-day adventure exploring Commencement Bay from the water and the shore!

Youth will depart from the CHB office aboard our boat for a bay patrol, stopping along the way to conduct real water quality testing and help record water color data for ongoing monitoring efforts. Next, they ll get up close with the bay s smallest residents during a plankton sampling session, using nets and microscopes to see what s living beneath the surface.
The adventure continues at Owen Beach, where kids will join in a Green Crab Molt Search — helping track this invasive species by combing the shoreline for shed crab shells — before refueling with a provided lunch by the water. Then it s back aboard for the cruise home to the CHB office.

Kids will leave with real hands-on science experience, a better understanding of the bay they call home, and a taste of what it means to protect it.

This program is FREE! Lunch is provided.

Ages 10–16
Friday, October 23 | 12:30 PM – 4:30 PM
Departs and returns from the CHB office
⚓ Spots are very limited due to boat capacity — sign up today!

This special concert introduces audiences to that enduring tradition through two artists who bring their own distinctive voices to the stage. Kim Soo Chan is one of Korea s most charismatic young trot entertainers, recognized for his appearances on Mr. Trot, Hidden Singer 2, and Active King of Singers 2. Combining powerful vocals with energetic choreography, playful humor, and impressions of legendary Korean singers, he brings a vibrant spirit to every performance. His engaging stage presence gives classic trot a fresh appeal while honoring the music that audiences have loved for decades. Through appearances on Miss Trot 2 and Active King of Singers, she won audiences over with her expressive voice, heartfelt delivery, and deep appreciation for Korean music. Comfortable communicating in both Korean and English, she offers a warm welcome to longtime trot fans and those discovering the genre for the first time. Together, Kim Soo Chan and Maria celebrate the growing international appeal of Korean trot—music rooted in tradition and brought to life with personality, passion, and contemporary energy. For Korean-American audiences, the evening offers a connection to familiar sounds and cherished memories. For new listeners, it opens the door to a rich and spirited musical world. title: Live at the Eleanor with Jazz Therapy
description: Jazz Therapy : This Christmas A Soulful Jazz Celebration – Featuring the music of This Christmas, plus soulful songs and gospel selections — Donny Hathaway, Stevie Wonder, The Carpenters, and The Preacher s Wife. THE BAND Teal Warren – Bass Pete Yankeh – Drums Henry Nielsen – Piano Bill Throssell – Trumpet & Flugel Horn Jon Fotheringill – Alto & Tenor Saxophone SPECIAL GUEST VOCALISTS Alma Villegas Cathy Satava In the vibrant tapestry of sound, where rhythm meets soul, Jazz Therapy emerges as a powerful force of musical healing. Born from the depths of rich jazz tradition and a passion for emotional expression, this dynamic ensemble brings an unparalleled fusion of soulful melodies, intricate rhythms, and exuberant improvisation that captivate audiences of all ages. Leader and visionary Teal Warren, renowned for his mastery of the bass and a deep-rooted passion for jazz as both a musician and army veteran, guides Jazz Therapy with an intuitive sense of harmony and collaboration. Drawing inspiration from many jazz legends, the ensemble creates a sonic universe where each note resonates with vibrant energy, inviting listeners to not only hear but to feel the music s transformative power. Collaborating with a talented lineup of seasoned musicians, Jazz Therapy is about more than just music—it s an experience. From the pulsing beats of slap bass to the gentle caress of a saxophone solo, every performance is a journey that fosters connection, reflection, and empowerment. This sense of unity is the bedrock of the band s philosophy, which centers on music as an innovative therapy — a sanctuary where individuals can come together, heal, and grow. With accolades that span esteemed jazz festivals and high-profile events, Jazz Therapy s eclectic repertoire seamlessly weaves in influences from modern jazz, blues, and world music, crafting a sound that s both a nod to the classics and a fresh auditory exploration. Each performance is an opportunity to not only entertain but to touch hearts and ignite spirits with the transformative magic of jazz. Jazz Therapy invites you to dive into their world, where music is the remedy and every performance is a soulful recollection of the universal language that binds us all. Whether you are a jazz connoisseur or a curious soul seeking refuge through sound, Jazz Therapy is exceptional, unforgettable, and ready to heal. Live at The Eleanor offers a cozy candlelit lounge experience where each performance unfolds like a conversation between artist and audience. Full bar and concessions are available; all ages are welcome.

title: Polyrhythmics
description: Funk-soul-R&B-jazz-Afrobeat Polyrhythmics For those whove ever wondered what Massive Attack would sound like doing bong hits with Miles Davis - The Georgia Straight Seattle-based Polyrhythmics are celebrating 16 years of sonic exploration following the release of their latest album, Life from Below (2025). Since forming in 2010, this six piece powerhouse has redefined instrumental music with a sound that blends funk, soul, psychedelic rock, R&B, and Afrobeat into a kaleidoscope of rhythm and groove. Known for their dynamic live performances and innovative compositions, the band has earned a reputation as one of the most captivating acts on the contemporary music scene. Polyrhythmics emerged from the rich creative soil of Seattles eclectic music community, releasing their self-titled debut album in 2011. Since then, their discography has grown to include fan-favorite albums such as Octagon (2015), Caldera (2017), Man from the Future (2020), and Life From Below (2025). Each release showcases their fearless exploration of genre boundaries and their commitment to crafting vibrant, deeply textured soundscapes. Last years Life From Below marked an exciting chapter for Polyrhythmics, delivering a fresh collection of grooves infused with the bold creativity and signature tight-knit musicianship that fans have come to expect. The band reflects on over a decade and a half of musical evolution, countless miles on the road, and a loyal community of listeners that continues to grow. Over the years, Polyrhythmics have graced stages at major festivals and renowned venues across the United States and internationally, sharing bills with legendary artists while carving out a distinct space in the global funk and soul scene. Their music - equal parts danceable, thoughtful, and immersive - offers a rich listening experience that draws from the roots of American funk and soul while incorporating global influences. As Polyrhythmics continue their journey, they remain committed to pushing boundaries, creating new grooves, and bringing their celebrated live energy to audiences around the world. Somatic Sundays are a gentle weekly space to reconnect with your body, nourish your nervous system, and settle into deeper presence. Each Sunday offers two practices that honor rhythm, breath, and inner awareness, with options for all levels and all bodies.

Class 1 — Mala Yoga: Mantra + 27 Sun & Moon Salutations (2:30PM-4PM)

We begin with Mala Yoga, a moving meditation that blends mantra, breath, and repetition to create steady rhythm in the body and mind.

The sequence unfolds in three parts:

1. 9 repetitions of a Sun mantra to awaken warmth, clarity, and activation.

2. Sun salutations, practiced with mindful pacing and accessible modifications.

3. 9 repetitions of a Moon mantra to soften, cool, and ground the energy.

4. Moon salutations, practiced slowly to invite spaciousness and emotional ease.

In total, we complete 27 sun and moon salutations, but always at a pace that honors your body. You are welcome to adapt movements, take breaks, or rest as needed. This is a practice of presence, not performance.

Class 2 — Qi Gong (4:15PM-5:45PM)

Our second offering is a spacious 90-minute Qi Gong class designed to support grounding, circulation, and emotional balance through gentle, flowing movement. We begin with the Five-Sound Healing practice — a simple, accessible way to release tension and support the organs using breath and sound.

After this grounding opening, we move into a full Qi Gong practice, exploring slow, fluid movements that are kind to the joints, beginner-friendly, and supportive for anyone needing a gentle somatic doorway into the week. The emphasis is on comfort, breath, and moving with ease.

You re welcome to join for one or both sessions.

Come as you are, and leave feeling centered, open, and deeply nourished.

title: Tacoma s Chinese Expulsion of 1885
description: On November 3, 1885, five hundred white Tacomans rounded up hundreds of the citys remaining Chinese residents and forcibly marched them through the pouring rain to a railroad station and crammed them into boxcars bound for Portland. After terrorizing local businessmen known to be supporters of the Chinese, this mob burned Tacomas Chinatown to the ground. The mob was so methodical in its expulsion of Chinese residents, local newspapers reported, that its approach was hailed as the Tacoma Method. Tacomas Chinese Expulsion was the dark culmination of national and local anti-Chinese sentiment, numerous outbursts of violence in the Puget Sound region, and a culture within the city of Tacoma that reinforced xenophobia and an enduring nativism. The terrorism in Tacoma dehumanized an immigrant population and stimulated expulsions of Chinese communities in over two hundred West Coast and Northwest towns and cities between 1885 and 1887.

title: Teen Open Studio: Familiar Materials: Paper Squishies Thursday, 5:00pm - Free
description: NULL
big_desc: Event featured image, but exclude link Event content IMAGE QUICK FACTS Admission Free · No registration required Location TAM Studio , Tacoma Art Museum DESCRIPTION Come join us December 17, 5–7pm for our Familiar Materials: Paper Squishies in Teen Open Studio! In artist Martha Parrish Bush s Dangle Twisty sculpture, found in TAM s Legacy: Highlights from the Permanent Collection exhibition, she is drawn to familiar and tactile materials like yarn and fabric. Today we are going to use materials familiar to us like construction paper and tape to create our own tactile piece of art in the form of a DIY paper squishy! Martha Parrish Bush, Dangle Twisty , 1995, crocheted yarn, 41 × 48 in. Gift of Herb and Lucy Pruzan, 2013.22.2 The project is a unique space for young minds to explore their creativity, connect with peers, and embrace the joy of self-expression. The schedule provides an array of hands-on artmaking activities. Every session, from painting and drawing to crafts, is a chance to discover new techniques and mediums. We will have some squishy giveaways (while supplies last), and a fidget trading station for anyone who wants to trade their paper squishies or fidgets with others! LOOK CLOSELY KNOW BEFORE YOU GO Know before you go: Drop in anytime from 5–7pm. All materials are provided. This program takes place during Free Thursday Neighborhood Nights , when admission to TAM is free from 5–8pm. ACCESSIBILITY For accessibility information, see Accessibility at TAM → ABOUT THE ARTIST → About the Artist: Martha Parrish Bush Martha Parrish Bush (born Chicago, Illinois, 1963) received her BFA from the University of Kansas, Lawrence and her MFA from the University of Washington. She taught at the University of Washington and North Seattle Community College, then went on to positions in Michigan and Connecticut. She trained as a painter but works across media. I had just returned from living abroad in Japan teaching ESL and studying traditional arts, ceramics, ikebana and paper making in Matsue, Japan. I was trying to make sense (probably) of the experiences I d had there. In Japan, the age old forms and traditions of making things were finely honed and honored and it got me thinking what I had been taught just simply by what was around me, what did I see, what had I grown up seeing around me — what were the traditional arts of the mid-west around the 1960 s, 70 s and 80 s from my eyes? What came to me was a tactile quality of materials, mostly fabrics, yarns and various craft materials; I knew what these felt like and they had a voice in my hands. I started collecting various handmade craft items from the shelves of various Salvation Army shops. I just let these things have a place in my studio. I loved the colors and the intricate patterns of the crochet work and the personal story acrylic yarn has was rooted into my sense of touch from an early age. The shapes I was trying to paint on canvas pushed out into space and began to claim size, multiples and attitude. Parts of the story that came with the materials worked with my sense of humor and also with my sense of placement and vantage point. The work took on a playful and child-like voice, sneaky with meaning or in your face bold. Artist statement courtesy of marthaparrishbush.com TRY IT AT HOME → Try It at Home: Paper Squishies Suggested materials: markers, colored pencils, scratch paper, construction paper, clear packing tape, rulers, scissors, and polyfill stuffing. Grab a piece of paper and trace out the shape you want your squishy to be. (Design your own or use a printed template!) Use your scissors to cut out the shape for the front and back of your squishy. Once you have your paper shapes, use markers or color pencils to color and add designs to your squishy. Cut a piece of packing tape that s at least 4 inches longer than your squishy is wide. Place the tape onto the paper so it s overlapping both the top and the sides; repeat until you reach the bottom of your paper. Cut off some of the excess tape, following the shape of the squishy and leaving about an inch along each side. Flip it over and attach the back side of the squishy, cover back with tape, still leaving the bottom open. Stuff your paper squishy with polyfill stuffing and then use tape to close the bottom. Now you have a complete paper squishy! ABOUT THE SERIES About the Series Teen Open Studio Teen Open Studio is a relaxed, creative space where teens can explore and express themselves through art. Participants have access to a variety of materials and receive supportive guidance from teaching artists and museum educators. Whether teens are working on personal projects, experimenting with new techniques, or trying art for the first time, the studio offers a welcoming environment for creative exploration, self-expression, and peer connection, encouraging artistic risk-taking, collaboration, and skill-building in a safe space to grow confidence. description: NULL
big_desc: Event featured image, but exclude link Event content IMAGE Hanging on for a safe pink day , MC, 2026 QUICK FACTS Admission Free · No registration required Location TAM Studio , Tacoma Art Museum DESCRIPTION Many artists use materials and colors to process emotions. David Hytone s exhibition , currently on view at Tacoma Art Museum, touches on this approach: The compartmentalization used as a coping mechanism in my day-to-day dovetails all too well with society s normalization of the latest tragic headline. —David Hytone Navigating rigid social expectations alongside the seasonal shift into darker winter days places a heavy emotional load on teenagers. Needle felting offers a direct, hands-on way to work through those pressures. Why needle felting works as a coping skill Vibrant Color Therapy: As daylight hours shrink and seasonal affective shifts kick in, working directly with rich, highly saturated, tactile colors (sun-warmed yellows, vibrant corals, deep forest greens) provides a rich sensory counterweight to gray winter afternoons. Sensory Grounding: Working with soft, natural wool engages tactile senses, pulling teens out of anxious thought loops and into the present moment. Art prompts for needle felting Pick three colors that represent the warmth or energy you miss most during dark winter days. Notice the sound and resistance as the needle enters the foam. How does it feel to physically push against that resistance? KNOW BEFORE YOU GO Know before you go: Drop in anytime from 5–7pm. All materials are provided. The Pilgrimage – Paulo Coehlo (288 pages)

The Pilgrimage by Paulo Coelho is a spiritual travel narrative inspired by Coelho s journey along the road to Santiago de Compostela in Spain. Blending memoir, allegory, and philosophical reflection, the book follows a quest for wisdom that would later shape the themes of The Alchemist: destiny, discipline, faith, and the search for meaning. It is less a conventional travel book than a symbolic journey through doubt, ritual, and self-discovery.

A spiritual journey across Spain that asks what we are really seeking when we travel.

Paulo Coelho is a Brazilian novelist best known internationally for The Alchemist. Born in Rio de Janeiro in 1947, he has written fiction shaped by spirituality, symbolism, and the search for personal meaning. His experience walking the road to Santiago became the basis for The Pilgrimage.

Written with Christie s dry wit and observational clarity, the book follows her experiences alongside her husband, archaeologist Max Mallowan, on excavation sites in the Middle East. Agatha Christie was one of the most widely read crime writers of the twentieth century, best known for Hercule Poirot, Miss Marple, and a vast body of detective fiction. title: Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism 2026
description: The Chinese Reconciliation Project Foundation invites the public to join them and the Washington State Historical Museum at the 2026 Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism. This annual demonstration r…
big_desc:
The Chinese Reconciliation Project Foundation invites the public to join them and the Washington State Historical Museum at the 2026 Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism. This annual demonstration retraces and reverses the walking path of expulsion forced on Tacomas Chinese American population in 1885, reclaiming the City for all peoples and cultures.

The walk, led by civic, educational, business and faith leaders, will begin near Union Station, where the Chinese pioneers in 1885 were marched at gunpoint out of town. Walkers will proceed north, led by Chinese Lion Dancers, through downtown Tacoma where many Chinese, and later Japanese businesses and houses once stood, along Schuster Parkway and the railroad- largely built by Chinese labor, and finally arrive at the Chinese Reconciliation Park. Throughout the walk, attendees will be within a half mile of the Northwest ICE Processing Center (NWIPC) where a similar white nationalist agenda continues to be orchestrated.

This year, the Opening Ceremony will take place inside the Washington State History Museums Mt. Tahoma Auditorium at 10 AM. After brief remarks from our Emcee and guest speaker, the Walk will begin from outside the Union Station around 10:45 AM. Walkers will arrive at the Chinese Reconciliation Park by 12 PM, and the event will conclude with final remarks, performances, and refreshments. To learn more about our guest speakers and our events timing, please visit our website.

Event Timing

  • Welcome Speeches begin at 10 AM, in the Washington State History Museum s Mt. Tahoma Auditorium.
  • The walk begins at 11 AM, from the History Museum s auditorium to the Tacoma Chinese Reconciliation Park.
  • The Conclusion Ceremony begins at 12:30 PM, at the Tacoma Chinese Reconciliation Park, featuring remarks from local dignitaries, a performance, and refreshments.

This event is free, open to all and families and children are most welcome. Join us in solidarity on Saturday, October 24th as we commit ourselves to anti-racism in the City of Destiny

Bus Schedule

To ensure our Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism is inclusive and accessible to all, we have organized a bus to transport participants who are unable to walk the three mile distance from the Union Station to the Tacoma Chinese Reconciliation Park.

  • The bus leaves the Union Station area at 10:45 AM, to transport attendees to the Chinese Reconciliation Park
  • The bus back leaves the Chinese Reconciliation Park at 1:15 PM, bringing attendees back to the Union Station.

History of The Tacoma Method

November 3, 2026, is the 141st anniversary of the 1885 expulsion of all remaining Chinese residents of Tacoma (possibly as many as 200 people). Many Chinese had left earlier that fall because of the hostile atmosphere here in Tacoma. The Chinese Must Go campaign was not an official act of the City government, but it was openly instigated and organized by elected officials (including the mayor and members of the City Council) and other leading citizens of civic influence. Soon after the event, the expulsion became known as the Tacoma Method in a rising tide of anti-Chinese sentiment and acts of violence in the western United States.

Join us in solidarity on Saturday, October 24th as we commit ourselves to anti-racism in the City of Destiny.

For more information, visit crpftacoma.org or contact Ben Everett at info@crpftacoma.org.

Participants will enjoy a guided walk through the park s forested trails, discovering the incredible diversity of wild mushrooms and native plants that thrive in the Pacific Northwest. Along the way, we ll pause to observe, ask questions, and learn how these organisms play a vital role in our local ecosystems.
